description_full: Vista Energy, S.A.B. de C.V., through its subsidiaries, engages in the exploration and production of oil and gas in Latin America. The company's principal assets is situated in the Vaca Muerta play, Neuquina basin, Argentina. It owns producing assets in Argentina and Mexico. In addition, the company involved in drilling and workover activities situated in Argentina. The company was formerly known as Vista Oil & Gas, S.A.B. de C.V. and changed its name to Vista Energy, S.A.B. de C.V. in April 2022. Vista Energy, S.A.B. de C.V. was incorporated in 2017 and is based in Mexico City, Mexico.
ceo_bio: Mr. Miguel Matias Galuccio | Founder, Chairman & CEO | Age 56
culture_narrative: Employs approximately 584 people. Revenue per employee of $2.8M ranks in the above the sector median among Energy peers, improving at 32%/yr — growing workforce leverage.
financial_summary: Vista Energy S.A.B. de C.V. is a mid-cap energy business with a $6.4B market cap on $1.6B of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +36% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder. Operating margins are expanding by +6.9pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.
Returns on capital run at 26% against a 8% cost of capital — a 18-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat, with gross margins sitting at 45%.
The company is burning through $94M of cash, and without positive owner earnings any valuation rests on hope rather than evidence.
Accruals are elevated at -11.4% of assets, and Sloan showed firms building earnings through accruals rather than cash systematically underperform.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 0.6× net debt/EBITDA, and interest coverage runs at 10.0×.

Shareholder yield is only 1.6%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 12% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and within its sector the business captures 3.5× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.

sect: Its 38% operating margin runs 22pp above the Energy median (16%), a real cost or pricing edge over peers.
It captures 3.48x its revenue share in sector profits, taking a disproportionate slice of the profit pool.
Over five years it has been gaining share of the sector profit pool (+88.3% a year).
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.05 across 202 companies in the universe; the top four hold 40% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares are in a strong uptrend, up 37% over the past year excluding the latest month, though it has pulled back 14% over the last three months.
The price sits mid-way through its 52-week range, 29% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 45% and a beta of 0.84, it moves roughly with the market, though its beta has shifted (1y -0.53 vs 5y 0.67), so read it loosely.
About $67.9M trades a day, enough to build a position.
In past sell-offs it fell 77% in the 2020 crash and 37% in the 2022 bear market.
val: The price sits above its DCF fair value of $51.90 (margin of safety -11%), so there is no valuation cushion.
The fair-value models corroborate one another (dispersion 4%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $32.22 to $84.60 (P10-P90).
On multiples it looks cheap against Energy peers: P/E 8.1 vs 13.4 and EV/EBITDA 3.7 vs 6.9 (sector median).
Against its own history it is dear: the EBIT multiple sits 103% above its 10-year median.
Earnings yields are thin: an FCF yield of -1.5% (below the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 6.6% (vs the 8% bar).
The 12 covering analysts target $95.32 on average, 66% above the price, well away from the model's fair value.
prof: ROIC of 26% clears the cost of capital of 8.2% by 18pp, the mark of a value creator; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 1.04).
It runs a 45% gross margin and burns cash (FCF margin -6%).
Earnings quality is mixed: cash conversion of 2.01x, but high accruals (-11.4% of assets).
ROE of 29% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (2.6x equity multiplier).
Operating margin is running 13pp above its own historical average, a peak-margin risk if conditions normalise.
hlth: Leverage is conservative at 0.6x net debt to EBITDA ($764.9M of cash against $1.4B of debt), with interest covered 10.0x.
The current ratio of 0.99 means short-term liabilities exceed current assets.
growth: Revenue has compounded at 36.2% over 3 years and 31.7% over 5 years, so growth is accelerating, and it has been lumpy (year-to-year swings of 59%).
At current returns, reinvesting 100% of profits supports about 26.3% a year of fundamental growth, enough to sustain growth.
It has missed earnings estimates by 22.4% on average.
Analysts expect 13.7% long-term annual earnings growth.
own: Insiders own 12.0%, meaningful skin in the game, and institutions hold 63%.
Shareholder yield is a modest 1.6% (1.6% in buybacks).
The share count has grown 1.8% a year over five years, diluting existing holders.
people: With about 584 employees, each generates about $2.8M of revenue, 1.4x the Energy median, and productivity has risen 31.7% a year.
Free cash flow is negative, at -$160K per employee.
The company is founder-led, which often keeps management aligned with long-term owners.
